definition: LNG is non-toxic, non-corrosive, and evaporates quickly without leaving residue when spilled; it is only flammable within a narrow 5-15 percent air-concentration band, so open-air spills pose low explosion risk compared with confined-space accumulation.
core_idea: Rapid evaporation plus a narrow flammability window mean LNG carries meaningfully less fire risk than storing oil or coal, though risk still exists if gas becomes trapped and concentrated in an enclosed space.
key_points: Aside from being extremely cold, LNG is non-toxic and non-corrosive.
Spilled LNG evaporates rapidly and leaves no residue.
Natural gas ignites only within a 5-15% concentration-in-air range.
Confined spaces (e.g., a house or storage facility) are where dangerous concentrations can build up.
Author states natural gas storage carries less fire risk than oil or coal storage facilities.
caveats: Any large volume of flammable material carries some fire risk, but the author distinguishes LNG as lower-risk than oil/coal, not risk-free.
